messages.subject: RStan: Confusing that model runs but does not update if warmup=0
parts:
You may want to add a stop condition preventing this? It took me a while to figure out that my model code actually was fine, but warmup=0 didn't make sense.

Thanks!
Thomas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] RStan: Confusing that model runs but does not update if warmup=0
parts:
warmup=0 should do just that --- take 0 warmup steps and
get right to sampling. For instance, this works as intended:

fit <- stan(model_code = "parameters { real y; } model { y ~ normal(0,1); }",
warmup=0);

Is it not doing that?

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] RStan: Confusing that model runs but does not update if warmup=0
parts:
Thanks, your model runs fine with warmup = 0, and I understand it's not a general issue.

In the following fit2 doesn't update (while fit1 does), and I suspect the root of the issue lies at the  R/C++ interaction on my machine.

fit1 <- stan(model_code = "data {real y[200]; } parameters { real mu; } model {y ~ normal(mu,1); }",
            data = list(y=rnorm(200)),
            warmup=10, iter=20,chains=2);
fit2 <- stan(model_code = "data {real y[200]; } parameters { real mu; } model {y ~ normal(mu,1); }",
            data = list(y=rnorm(200)),
            warmup=0, iter=10,chains=2, verbose=T);
